sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: RabbitMQ interview questions cover the AMQP-based broker still common in finance, telco and any Java backend that needs flexible routing — exchange types (direct, fanout, topic, headers), bindings and routing keys, queue durability and message persistence, dead-letter exchanges and DLQ patterns, prefetch and consumer ack strategies, publisher confirms, clustering and quorum queues, and the Spring AMQP integration patterns. Use this page when the role specifies RabbitMQ over Kafka.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
RabbitMQ = **AMQP broker** with rich routing.

- **Exchanges** route — direct / topic / fanout / headers.
- **Queues** durable + persistent + manual ack ⇒ at-least-once.
- **Quorum queues** (3.8+) replace mirrored queues — Raft-replicated.
- **Prefetch** + manual ack tunes throughput vs fairness.
- **DLX** (dead-letter exchange) catches poison messages.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
The interview surface for this module breaks into these focus areas:

- **Rabbitmq fundamentals** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Manual ack** — no ack ⇒ redelivery on consumer crash; classic interview trap.
- **Publisher confirms** — at-least-once on the publish side.
- **Quorum vs classic** — Raft vs single-master; pick quorum for new clusters.
- **Topic exchange wildcards** — `*` one word, `#` zero+ words.
- **Backpressure** — close to publish-side at the connection level when consumers fall behind.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I'd use a topic exchange routed on `<context>.<event>`, durable + quorum queues, manual ack with prefetch tuned, publisher confirms on the producer, and a DLX bound to a parking queue for ops to inspect."*
